# Embroidery Digitization

Curated by Skill Harbor — encodes the practical knowledge a digitizer applies when turning a vector design into machine-embroidery stitch parameters: the per-element decision flow (stitch type → direction → spacing → underlay → push/pull compensation → trims), satin width thresholds, fabric-specific starting numbers (stable woven to fleece and leather), underlay strategies, color/needle ordering rules, a trim-and-jump decision rubric with a measured trims-vs-density trade table, visual failure modes from stitch-plan previews, a small-detail survival guide, and three ready starting recipes (T-shirt logo, patch, fleece). Designed to pair with the cli-anything-inkstitch skill. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @bobbymarko. Honest caveats: embroidery is empirical — every number is a starting point, always sample-stitch before a final run; you need Ink/Stitch installed (free) and an embroidery machine for real output; 7 installs on the catalog, but popularity is not a review. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
